text: A living archive of thermal instability The Art of Thermal InstabilityRediscover the physics. Recreate the figures. From the first unstable wave to a two-phase medium. Explore the equations, reproduce the figures, and follow the gas into nonlinear evolution. Choose a starting pointAbout this calculation 2D compressible thermal condensation · 256 × 160 KI-type cooling · deliberately enhanced conduction Illustrative model; no sustained turbulence or paper reproduction claimed. Three ways into the physics Start with a paper, a movie, or a calculation. Follow the original sources, see the gas evolve, or run a small published example. Field (1965): thermal conduction and the unstable scales. Recomputed from the published equation and numerically checked; not a point-by-point digitization of the printed figure. Browse the full paper and book atlas · Check what is validated, provisional or planned The unit of this archive Study the figure. Read the equations. Run the code. Published exhibits state their physics, numerical setup and validation scope. Follow the code and data where available, and distinguish a recomputed equation, an illustrative model and an unresolved historical match. The full atlas also marks references and future work. From the original movie archive See the historical simulations move. Four 2D and four 3D recordings of thermal instability, two-phase gas, shocks and MHD, with an edited 3D introduction. Quality and provenance notes accompany each clip. Open the movie gallery Detail from an archived 3D shock movie. View the recording. 01 / Paper and book atlas From the classics to current simulations. All references in chronological order, oldest first. Topic filters preserve this order. Field’s three figures and the corrected KI equilibrium benchmark. Historical models and front calculations retain explicit prototype limits. 47 references · oldest first · 7 exhibits numerically validated 1953 Reference listed · scope proposed Eugene N. Parker Instability of Thermal Fields Thermal-field stability before Field (1965), with a solar-atmosphere application. Proposed scope Historical background: compare the temperature-field equation, conduction, and heating assumptions with Field’s hydrodynamic analysis. Keep the original solar application distinct from neutral interstellar gas. Historical theory & heating sources →Paper & bibliography ↗ 1960 Source rates audited · truncated model Takayanagi & Nishimura Cooling of the Interstellar Clouds in Region of Neutral Hydrogen H₂ rotational excitation and the cooling budget of neutral clouds. About this exhibit 34 printed upward H + para-H2 rates audited on p. 82; a truncated steady level calculation is compared with 60 printed cooling values. Twelve numerical checks pass, while the largest Table 2 discrepancy is retained at about 21.72%. H₂ rates & cooling comparison →Rate-coefficient lineage & scope →Paper & bibliography ↗ 1961 Reference listed · scope proposed Hayakawa, Nishimura & Takayanagi Radiations from the Interstellar Hydrogen Atoms Excitation and ionization of interstellar hydrogen by suprathermal particles, connecting radiation and cloud heating. Proposed scope Audit particle spectra, excitation/ionization definitions, and radiation/heating yields separately from thermally averaged chemical rates. Rate-coefficient lineage & scope →Paper & bibliography ↗ 1961 Reference listed · scope proposed S. Chandrasekhar Hydrodynamic and Hydromagnetic Stability Buoyancy-driven thermal convection and its Boussinesq approximation: a fluid-dynamical comparison with radiative thermal instability. Proposed scope Proposed entry point: the onset of convection in a layer heated from below, followed by a neutral Rayleigh curve for explicitly specified mechanical and thermal boundaries. Retain velocity, perturbation pressure and buoyancy; distinguish this mechanism from the Field radiative-condensation mode. No equation or figure reproduction yet. Boussinesq convection & scope →Book & bibliography ↗ 1965 Numerically validated George B. Field Thermal Instability Explore the conditions for condensation through linear theory. About this exhibit Figures 1–3: stability domains, condensation growth (alpha=1/2), and wave growth (alpha=-2), with gamma=5/3. Equation-based reproductions with 15 map checks, 10 condensation checks, and 24 wave checks. Printed boundaries and curves have not been digitized for a pointwise comparison. Figure 1: stability map →Figure 2: condensation →Figure 3: waves →Paper & bibliography ↗ 1968 Reference listed · scope proposed Spitzer & Tomasko Heating of H I Regions by Energetic Particles Energetic-particle heating and ionization of H I, including secondary-electron energy deposition and metal cooling. Proposed scope Prioritize the definitions of primary/total ionization rates and energy per ionization when comparing with FGH/GHF. Audit secondary-electron treatment, abundances, and collider channels before implementing a heating benchmark. Historical theory & heating sources →Paper & bibliography ↗ 1969 Historical match unresolved · deferred Field, Goldsmith & Habing Cosmic-Ray Heating of the Interstellar Gas From heating and cooling balance to two coexisting phases. About this exhibit Historical heating/cooling diagnostics and cold-to-warm prototype, now compared with96 sparse readings of Figures1/2. Warm pressure maximum1516.7 versus printed1800Kcm^-3; larger local differences remain near the shifted transition. Historical coefficient recovery is deferred, without fitting a correction. Two-phase equilibrium prototype →Heating & cooling ingredients →Reduced cold branch →Original-figure comparison & stopping note →Paper & bibliography ↗ 1969 Reference listed · scope proposed Hattori, Nakano & Hayashi Thermal and Dynamical Evolution of Gas Clouds of Various Masses Gas-cloud evolution with molecular/atomic line cooling, grains, radiation, and ionization in transparent and opaque regimes. Proposed scope Inventory the individual heating/cooling prescriptions and their cited atomic/molecular data before choosing a small thermal-evolution calculation. Rate-coefficient lineage & scope →Paper & bibliography ↗ 1969 Reference listed · scope proposed Zel’dovich & Pikel’ner The Phase Equilibrium and Dynamics of a Gas Volume That Is Heated and Cooled Conductive interfaces select the stationary two-phase pressure; away from that pressure the boundary moves. Proposed scope Candidate: the planar saturation condition and a steady front or front-speed calculation. Specify the heat-loss law, conductivity, signs, and boundary conditions. Phase-transition front lineage →Paper & bibliography ↗ 1970 Reference listed · scope proposed Penston & Brown The Cloud–Intercloud Phase-Change in the Interstellar Medium Thermal balance across a conducting cloud–intercloud interface adds a condition beyond pressure balance. Proposed scope Candidate: compare the stationary interface criterion and thermal timescales with the Zel’dovich–Pikel’ner formulation before choosing a small front calculation. Phase-transition front lineage →Paper & bibliography ↗ 1972 Computed prototype · review pending Schwarz, McCray & Stein Formation of Clouds in a Cooling Interstellar Medium Thermal conduction and recombination shape perturbations growing in an isochorically cooling background. About this exhibit Early-time linear Figure2 plus a nonlinear3pc/10percent Lagrangian prototype without a Riemann solver. Historical-scale64/96/128-cell runs and a512-cell auxiliary comparison document conservation, timing/input differences, and unresolved conductive-front resolution. Cooling-medium condensation: Figure2 prototype →Nonlinear Lagrangian condensation →Paper & bibliography ↗ 1972 Reference listed · scope proposed Dalgarno & McCray Heating and Ionization of HI Regions A historical review of heating and ionization processes in neutral interstellar gas. Proposed scope Use as a source map for historical heating/cooling processes. Audit individual formulas, ionization fractions, abundance assumptions, and original rate references before selecting a cooling-curve calculation. Historical theory & heating sources →Paper & bibliography ↗ 1986 Reference listed · scope proposed Steven A. Balbus Local Dynamic Thermal Instability Local thermal-instability criteria for time-dependent background flows; transport processes are omitted in this analytical treatment. Proposed scope Compare the loss-per-unit-mass convention and the derivative of loss/T with Field’s equilibrium criterion. This is analytical background, not a conduction-resolved nonlinear simulation exhibit. Historical theory & heating sources →Paper & bibliography ↗ 1990 Reference listed · scope proposed Begelman & McKee Global Effects of Thermal Conduction on Two-Phase Media Thermal conduction transfers mass between phases through evaporation and condensation; a Field-length scale organizes the competition with heating and cooling. Proposed scope Audit the Field-length definition and the assumptions of classical conduction, uniform pressure, and small cloud filling factor. Compare reduced evolution equations while retaining the original thermal model and application. Historical theory & heating sources →Paper & bibliography ↗ 1991 Reference listed · scope proposed Nishi, Nakano & Umebayashi Magnetic Flux Loss from Interstellar Clouds with Various Grain-Size Distributions Ionization–recombination equilibrium with electrons, ions and charged grains; grain-size distributions affect magnetic coupling in shielded molecular clouds. Proposed scope Candidate: Figure1 charged-species abundances at10K for the standard MRN grain distribution, before comparing the other grain models. Recover the required reaction rates and PaperI inputs first. This is a charge-equilibrium benchmark, not a thermal-equilibrium curve or a reproduced magnetic-flux-loss calculation. Ionization, grain charge & proposed benchmark →Paper & bibliography ↗ 1992 Reference listed · scope proposed Elphick, Regev & Shaviv Dynamics of Fronts in Thermally Bistable Fluids Isobaric conductive fronts, a Lyapunov functional, equal-depth potential minima and interacting cloud boundaries. Proposed scope The source equations are reviewed; no numerical reproduction yet. Candidate: the cubic benchmark, static kink or front speed versus potential-depth difference, retaining the Lagrangian mass coordinate and state-dependent mobility. Front lineage & source review →Ginzburg–Landau connection →Paper & bibliography ↗ 1993 Reference listed · scope proposed Ferrara & Shchekinov Dynamics of Conductive/Cooling Fronts: Cloud Implosion and Thermal Solitons Conductive and radiative interfaces admit static and steady fronts, cloud compression, and soliton-like solutions. Proposed scope Start with planar static/steady front equations, boundary heat fluxes, and the mechanical analogy. Select a small ODE benchmark after auditing the heat-loss law, conductivity, and pressure/flow assumptions. Cloud implosion simulations are a separate, optional scope. Planar fronts & steady flow →Paper & bibliography ↗ 1994 Reference listed · scope proposed Bakes & Tielens The Photoelectric Heating Mechanism for Very Small Graphitic Grains and Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons Photoelectric heating by small carbonaceous grains and PAHs, including grain charging and a heating-efficiency prescription. Proposed scope Trace the photoelectric-heating input used in later neutral-gas models. Audit radiation-field normalization, electron density, grain population, temperature range, and net gas–grain energy exchange before plotting the efficiency fit. Historical theory & heating sources →Paper & bibliography ↗ 1995 Reference listed · scope proposed Wolfire, Hollenbach, McKee, Tielens & Bakes The Neutral Atomic Phases of the Interstellar Medium Photoelectric heating by small grains and PAHs, X-ray/cosmic-ray ionization, and atomic phase equilibrium. Proposed scope Audit the heating/cooling terms and identify a local equilibrium curve for a modest-cost calculation. Research path & scope →Paper & bibliography ↗ 1999 Reference listed · scope proposed Hennebelle & Pérault Dynamical condensation in a thermally bistable flow. Application to interstellar cirrus Transonic converging warm flows produce cold condensations; self-similar non-isobaric solutions describe early condensation. Proposed scope Audit the self-similar solution and size/velocity thresholds versus ambient pressure. Start with analytic relations or a planar one-dimensional benchmark; preserve the original heating/cooling and boundary conditions. Condensation, turbulence & fragmentation →Paper & bibliography ↗ 2000 Planned Koyama & Inutsuka Molecular Cloud Formation in Shock-Compressed Layers From shock-compressed layers to molecular cloud formation. View planned exhibit Locate original code and data, then select target figures and define the scope of a new implementation. Paper & bibliography ↗ 2000 Reference listed · scope proposed Hennebelle & Pérault Dynamical condensation in a magnetized and thermally bistable flow. Application to interstellar cirrus Oblique magnetic fields and tension alter condensation in slab geometry; transverse motions can align fields or flows and permit compression. Proposed scope Compare nonmagnetic, transverse-field, and oblique-field limits using the published self-similar analysis and a small one-dimensional MHD benchmark. Audit the angle and field-strength assumptions before choosing a figure. Condensation, turbulence & fragmentation →Paper & bibliography ↗ 2000 Reference listed · scope proposed Burkert & Lin Thermal Instability and the Formation of Clumpy Gas Clouds During radiative cooling, the transition from isobaric to isochoric evolution limits perturbation growth and influences the characteristic clump scale; conduction suppresses small scales. Proposed scope Audit the growth, transition-temperature, and nonlinear-amplitude estimates. Use small analytic or time-dependent perturbation calculations before considering fragmentation simulations; distinguish cooling backgrounds from thermal equilibrium. Condensation, turbulence & fragmentation →Paper & bibliography ↗ 2001 Reference listed · scope proposed Shchekinov & Ibáñez Interaction of Small Planar Perturbations with Cooling-Conductive Fronts Acoustic and entropy perturbations interact with steady subsonic cold–hot fronts in one-dimensional planar geometry, with heating, cooling, and thermal conduction. Proposed scope First audit the steady planar background and its mass-flux eigenvalue at prescribed pressure, as discussed by Iwasaki & Inutsuka (2012), section 3. Then consider reflection/transmission coefficients as a separate perturbation benchmark. Do not equate this one-dimensional perturbation problem with transverse front corrugation. Planar fronts & steady flow →Paper & bibliography ↗ 2002 Numerically validated Koyama & Inutsuka An Origin of Supersonic Motions in Interstellar Clouds Corrected heating/cooling law, thermal equilibria and local isobaric stability. About this exhibit Validated equilibrium benchmark, planar ZP saturation and pressure-dependent effective potential wells with explicit coordinates, normalization and independent quadrature checks; corrected coefficients traced to primary sources. Original 2D simulation remains outside this exhibit. Thermal equilibrium & ZP saturationPressure-dependent potential wells →Paper & bibliography ↗ 2003 Reference listed · scope proposed Wolfire, McKee, Hollenbach & Tielens Neutral Atomic Phases of the Interstellar Medium in the Galaxy Revised atomic-gas microphysics and the allowed two-phase pressure range across the Galactic disk. Proposed scope Compare physical inputs with the 1995 model before attempting an equilibrium calculation. Research path & scope →Paper & bibliography ↗ 2004 Planned Koyama & Inutsuka The Field Condition: A New Constraint on Spatial Resolution in Simulations of the Nonlinear Development of Thermal Instability Examine numerical convergence through thermal conduction and spatial resolution. View planned exhibit Candidate exhibits compare simulations with and without thermal conduction across different spatial resolutions. Paper & bibliography ↗ 2005 Reference listed · scope proposed Nagashima, Koyama & Inutsuka Evaporation and condensation of H I clouds in thermally bistable interstellar media: semi-analytic description of isobaric dynamics of curved interfaces Curvature modifies evaporation and condensation for cylindrical, spherical, and general fronts under an isobaric approximation. Proposed scope Candidate: evaluate the semi-analytic curvature correction and compare planar, cylindrical, and spherical limits using a small ODE calculation. Keep the polynomial heat-loss model distinct from later realistic fits. Phase-transition front lineage →Paper & bibliography ↗ 2005 Reference listed · scope proposed Audit & Hennebelle Thermal condensation in a turbulent atomic hydrogen flow Two-dimensional turbulent converging flows condense warm H I into cold structures; the thermally unstable gas fraction correlates with turbulence. Proposed scope Start with the semi-analytical model for unstable gas and its relation to turbulence. Reanalyse published diagnostics or available outputs after a provenance audit. A full high-resolution two-dimensional run is optional. Condensation, turbulence & fragmentation →Paper & bibliography ↗ 2006 Reference listed · scope proposed Inoue, Inutsuka & Koyama Structure and Stability of Phase Transition Layers in the Interstellar Medium CNM/WNM fronts, evaporation and condensation, and corrugational stability. Proposed scope Candidate: a plane-parallel front or the linear growth relation, after checking boundary conditions. Research path & scope →Paper & bibliography ↗ 2006 Reference listed · scope proposed Nagashima, Inutsuka & Koyama How Long Can Tiny H I Clouds Survive? Spherical cloud evaporation times depend on cloud size and ambient pressure, with a quasi-steady interpretation. Proposed scope Candidate: reproduce the analytic timescale/critical-radius relation and, if practical, a one-dimensional radial benchmark. Large multidimensional reruns are unnecessary for this scope. Phase-transition front lineage →Paper & bibliography ↗ 2006 Reference listed · scope proposed Koyama & Inutsuka Nonlinear Development of Thermal Instability without External Forcing Conduction, viscosity, and cloud motions in multidimensional nonlinear thermal instability without external forcing. Proposed scope Start with the preprint’s physical mechanism, diagnostics, and any available outputs. A full 2D/3D rerun is optional; its journal-publication status remains unverified. Phase-transition front lineage →Paper & bibliography ↗ 2006 Reference listed · scope proposed Heitsch, Slyz, Devriendt, Hartmann & Burkert The Birth of Molecular Clouds: Formation of Atomic Precursors in Colliding Flows Colliding atomic flows develop structure through dynamical and thermal instabilities before molecular hydrogen begins to form. Proposed scope Document the inflow, cooling law, geometry, and instability diagnostics. Prefer reanalysis of available density/temperature and fragmentation outputs; do not require a full multidimensional rerun or imply that this model follows the molecular stage. Condensation, turbulence & fragmentation →Paper & bibliography ↗ 2007 Reference listed · scope proposed Inoue, Inutsuka & Koyama The Role of Ambipolar Diffusion in the Formation Process of Moderately Magnetized Diffuse Clouds Two-fluid condensation and the competition between magnetic flux accumulation and ambipolar diffusion. Proposed scope Candidate: the analytic field-strength estimate or a small 1D verification case. Research path & scope →Paper & bibliography ↗ 2007 Reference listed · scope proposed Hennebelle & Audit On the structure of the turbulent interstellar atomic hydrogen. I. Physical characteristics. Influence and nature of turbulence in a thermally bistable flow High-resolution two-dimensional bistable turbulence produces small-scale CNM structures, a cloud mass spectrum, and distinct density and velocity statistics. Proposed scope Begin with the analytical mass-spectrum argument and definitions of the measured spectra. Recompute diagnostics only from accessible, documented outputs; retain the dimensionality dependence and avoid treating a small run as a reproduction of the full statistics. Condensation, turbulence & fragmentation →Paper & bibliography ↗ 2008 Reference listed · scope proposed Inoue & Inutsuka Two-Fluid MHD Simulations of Converging H I Flows in the Interstellar Medium. I: Methodology and Basic Results Two-fluid coupling and magnetic limits on condensation in converging atomic flows. Proposed scope Document the method and inputs; consider a coupling benchmark or analysis of available outputs rather than a full 2D rerun. Research path & scope →Paper & bibliography ↗ 2008 Reference listed · scope proposed Iwasaki & Tsuribe Self-similar solutions for the dynamical condensation of a radiative gas layer Non-equilibrium thermal condensation described by a family of plane-parallel similarity solutions. Proposed scope Candidate: similarity profiles and limiting scalings, using an ODE solver and a small 1D comparison. Research path & scope →Paper & bibliography ↗ 2008 Reference listed · scope proposed Heitsch, Hartmann & Burkert Fragmentation of Shocked Flows: Gravity, Turbulence, and Cooling Comparing dynamical, thermal, and gravitational timescales identifies where shocked flows fragment and seed local collapse. Proposed scope A timescale/regime diagram is a promising inexpensive reproduction target. First audit the cooling law, perturbation scales, background state, and boundaries; keep this calculation distinct from a full flow-driven cloud simulation. Condensation, turbulence & fragmentation →Paper & bibliography ↗ 2009 Reference listed · scope proposed Inoue & Inutsuka Two-Fluid MHD Simulations of Converging H I Flows in the Interstellar Medium. II: Are Molecular Clouds Generated Directly from a Warm Neutral Medium? The angle between inflow and mean magnetic field affects shocked atomic gas and cloud formation. Proposed scope Compare model assumptions and published diagnostics; reanalyse public outputs if available. Large runs are outside the initial scope. Research path & scope →Paper & bibliography ↗ 2009 Reference listed · scope proposed Iwasaki & Tsuribe Fragmentation of a dynamically condensing radiative layer Perturbation growth on a time-dependent, dynamically condensing background. Proposed scope Candidate: linear perturbation evolution on the time-dependent similarity solution, before a full nonlinear calculation. Research path & scope →Paper & bibliography ↗ 2012 Reference listed · scope proposed Inoue & Inutsuka Formation of Turbulent and Magnetized Molecular Clouds via Accretion Flows of H I Clouds Three-dimensional MHD with chemistry, conduction, and accretion of inhomogeneous atomic gas. Proposed scope Focus on setup documentation, analysis methods, and any available snapshots. Do not require rerunning the full 3D calculation. Research path & scope →Paper & bibliography ↗ 2012 Computed prototype · review pending Iwasaki & Inutsuka Structure of dynamical condensation fronts in the interstellar medium Condensation-front families parameterized by pressure and mass flux, with cooling- and Field-length regimes. About this exhibit Confirmed target: Figures 5 and 7, pressure–mass-flux classification. A computed prototype reproduces nine stated example classes and passes 30 checks. Unavailable CNM branches and temperature-limited cells are masked; the jcrit overlay and complete boundary comparison await technical review. Figures 5 & 7: computed prototype →Research path & scope →Paper & bibliography ↗ 2013 Reference listed · scope proposed Jeong-Gyu Kim & Woong-Tae Kim Instability of Evaporation Fronts in the Interstellar Medium Thermal conduction suppresses short-wavelength corrugations of CNM–WNM evaporation fronts. Linear stability analysis connects to nonlinear front deformation and enhanced evaporation. Proposed scope Detailed reconstruction of AppendixA with coupled eigenfunctions as the required output. Primary target: Figure9 temperature and transverse-velocity profiles from the same normalized mode; supporting targets are the background front, Figure5 dispersion and long-wave/cutoff limits. Source-audited plan only; no Kim eigenfunctions computed yet. Nonlinear2D remains separate and optional. Conductive evaporation-front stability →Eigenfunction reconstruction specification →Paper & bibliography ↗ 2014 Reference listed · scope proposed Iwasaki & Inutsuka Self-Sustained Turbulence without Dynamical Forcing: A Two-Dimensional Study of a Bistable Interstellar Medium Thermal conduction, phase transitions, viscosity, and kinetic-energy transfer in a bistable medium. Proposed scope Prioritize published energy budgets and analysis of available outputs. A small front problem can isolate the mechanism without reproducing the full 2D run. Research path & scope →Paper & bibliography ↗ 2017 Reference listed · scope proposed Gong, Ostriker & Wolfire A Simple and Accurate Network for Hydrogen and Carbon Chemistry in the Interstellar Medium A compact chemical network with an author-maintained public PDR implementation and rate corrections. Proposed scope Pin a corrected rate/code version, inspect units and validity ranges, then choose a small chemical or thermal benchmark. Research path & scope →Paper & bibliography ↗ 2019 Reference listed · scope proposed Iwasaki, Tomida, Inoue & Inutsuka The Early Stage of Molecular Cloud Formation by Compression of Two-phase Atomic Gases Three-dimensional MHD, non-equilibrium chemistry, and the critical magnetic-field/inflow angle for cloud formation. Proposed scope Candidate: evaluate the analytic critical-angle relation and reanalyse available outputs; full parameter-survey reruns are optional. Research path & scope →Paper & bibliography ↗ 2023 Reference listed · scope proposed Gong, Ho, Stone, Ostriker, Caselli, Grassi, C.-G. Kim, J.-G. Kim & Halevi Implementation of Chemistry in the Athena++ Code A public chemistry framework including GOW17, general KIDA networks, and coupled thermal/chemical evolution. Proposed scope Begin with published tests, public inputs, or a small one-zone/1D case; full 3D runs are optional. Research path & scope →Paper & bibliography ↗ Research paths Follow the physics into later work. Trace early atomic and molecular data through Takayanagi, Nishimura, Hayakawa, Hattori, Nakano, and Hayashi. Explore Wolfire’s phase-equilibrium models, GOW’s public chemistry, and Inoue and Iwasaki’s studies of fronts and magnetized clouds. For modern multidimensional simulations, the scope can be source documentation, available-data analysis, or a small physical benchmark; a full rerun is optional. A separate path follows Zel’dovich–Pikel’ner, Penston–Brown, and Nagashima’s front calculations. Reading list, public rates & computational scope → 02 / Beyond the papers Preserve the research beyond the papers. Research Notes Unpublished simulations, exploratory work, and open questions. Each note will record its purpose, setup, results, and validation status. Data Archive Trace each figure back to its calculation. Run identifiers, parameters, code versions, and units will form the basis of a searchable data catalog. Research notes and datasets will be released after the source material has been organized and the results validated. 03 / Release by release Build the archive, one release at a time. v0.1 The first Field exhibits Published on GitHub Pages with Figures 1–3, reproducible code, curve data, and validation. Published v0.2–0.3 Revisiting the classics FGH/GHF equilibrium curves and the linear and nonlinear Schwarz1972 calculations are available as prototypes. A96-point comparison documents the residual mismatch. Historical coefficient recovery is deferred pending specific new evidence. v0.4–0.6 Koyama & Inutsuka Revisit the 2000, 2002, and 2004 papers individually, connecting original materials with new implementations. v0.7–1.0 Research notes & data Organize unpublished and recent simulations, and release validated datasets.
